To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimum management regime is that which maximizes profit, and that this optimum regime can be determined by simulation of crop response to management, and optimization of the resulting profit function.

(1) the use of the optimal management regime for the crop enterprise will result in a yield that is 10% higher than the yield that would result if the farmer used his best judgment in managing the crop, (2) the use of a management regime that is 10-20% better than the farmer's best judgment will result in a 3-4% yield increase over the farmer's best yield.
The identification of optimum management regimes for annual crop enterprises is a computationally difficult problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing a computer-based decision-making aid for the management of agricultural crop enterprises.

the development of simulation models of the crop management decision process, and the application of these models to the development of management regimes which optimize the yield and profit of a crop.
the development of a computer-based decision support system to assist the farmer and agricultural advisor in the management of crop production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potential for a crop management optimization program is considerable.
there is a need for a crop management optimizing model, and that such a model is feasible.
the potential of simulation modelling in the area of agricultural crop management is enormous and that, with a little ingenuity, a crop management optimizing model could be constructed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are still in a very early phase in the development of crop management models.
the development of a management optimizing program is a worthwhile goal, but that the problems are not trivial.
the techniques of simulation and optimization are potentially applicable to the management of agricultural enterprises.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimization of agricultural production is possible, and that it is possible to devise a program that can be used in the field.
the use of a crop management optimization program can lead to improved crop management decisions, and hence to improved crop yields and profitability.
we have developed a new approach to crop management that can be used to optimize the management of crops.
